story: Before Edwin Hubble transformed cosmology, most astronomers believed our Milky Way galaxy was the entire universe. Born in Missouri in 1889, Hubble was a standout athlete who studied law at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar to satisfy his dying father's wishes. He worked as a high school Spanish teacher and served as a U.S. Army major during World War I before devoting himself to astronomy. In 1919, Hubble joined Mount Wilson Observatory, using the world's largest 100-inch Hooker Telescope. By observing Cepheid variable stars, he proved that the Andromeda Nebula was actually an independent galaxy far beyond our own. In 1929, he showed that distant galaxies are moving away from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance. This redshift discovery proved the universe is expanding, prompting Albert Einstein to retract his cosmological constant as his biggest blunder. Today, NASA's premier space telescope carries Hubble's name.
angle: Before Edwin Hubble's observations in the 1920s, humanity believed the Milky Way was the entire universe; Hubble proved space contains millions of separate galaxies in an ever-expanding cosmos.

claims.claim: Edwin Hubble was born in Marshfield, Missouri on November 20, 1889.
As an undergraduate at the University of Chicago, Hubble studied mathematics and astronomy.
Hubble was a gifted athlete in his youth, participating in sports including basketball, track, and boxing.
Hubble attended Oxford University as a Rhodes Scholar.
Hubble studied law at Oxford to fulfill a promise to his father.
After returning from Oxford, Hubble worked as a high school Spanish teacher in New Albany, Indiana.
Hubble served in the United States Army during World War I and achieved the rank of major.
In 1919, Hubble joined the staff at Carnegie's Mount Wilson Observatory in California.
At Mount Wilson, Hubble conducted observations with the 100-inch Hooker Telescope, the world's largest telescope at the time.
In the early 20th century, the prevailing scientific belief was that the Milky Way made up the entire universe.
Hubble used Cepheid variable stars to calculate distances to faint objects previously classified as nebulae.
Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered the relationship between a Cepheid variable star's brightness and its pulsation period used to measure space distances.
Hubble proved that the Andromeda Nebula was actually an independent galaxy located far outside the Milky Way.
Hubble observed that light emitted from distant galaxies was shifted toward the red end of the spectrum.
Hubble established that a galaxy's recession velocity increases proportionally with its distance from Earth, a relation known as Hubble's Law.
Hubble's observational data provided the foundational evidence that the universe is expanding.
Hubble developed the standard system used by astronomers to classify galaxies based on their shape.
Albert Einstein visited Mount Wilson in 1931 and publicly acknowledged that Hubble's expansion evidence changed his mind, calling his cosmological constant his biggest blunder.
Hubble did not win a Nobel Prize in Physics during his lifetime because astronomy was not an eligible category at the time.
The Hubble Space Telescope was named in Edwin Hubble's honor.

disputed: Hubble's Ph.D. completion year (S1 lists 1921, whereas S2 lists 1914): The script should omit the exact Ph.D. graduation year.

The claim that fight promoters offered Hubble a shot at world heavyweight champion Jack Johnson (S6 states promoters courted him to fight Johnson, S5 notes promoters 'reportedly' tried to get him to turn pro, while other biographies omit this): The script should omit this detail or explicitly attribute it as 'according to legend'.

Hubble's initial calculation of the age of the universe (S1 and S6 note his distance errors led to an estimated age of 2 billion years, far below today's accepted 13.8 billion years): The script should focus on the discovery of expansion rather than his precise initial age figure.

The US Postal Service stamp claim that Hubble would have won the 1953 Nobel Prize in Physics had he not died (S1 notes this assertion is likely false despite his nomination): The script should leave out this stamp citation.
